evidence.title: Kiro
evidence.finding: Distinguishes IDE/CLI/Web/mobile/Crew; cloud execution and cross-surface steering.

evidence.title: Specs
evidence.finding: Requirement/design/task files, dependency-wave scheduling and surface restrictions.

evidence.title: Installation
evidence.finding: Kiro documents distinct IDE, CLI, Web, iOS early access and Crew installations, with OS-specific requirements.

evidence.title: Mobile
evidence.finding: Kiro iOS is early access through TestFlight; detailed mobile documentation is still pending.

evidence.title: Specs
evidence.locator: Capability matrix; core structure; task execution
evidence.finding: Specs create requirements/design/tasks files and schedule independent tasks in dependency waves; correctness testing and mobile parity have explicit limits.

evidence.title: Cloud sessions
evidence.locator: How sessions work; prerequisites; client matrix
evidence.finding: Clients attach to the same remote session; disconnection does not stop work, approvals wait, and paid plans include cloud compute with a ten-session cap.

evidence.title: Kiro Web
evidence.finding: Web is a paid-plan cloud client with interactive, Spec and autonomous modes, cron schedules and a documented no-auto-merge boundary.

evidence.title: Steering
evidence.finding: Workspace and global steering have separate scopes; cloud use of local personal configuration requires opt-in upload.

evidence.title: Crew quick start
evidence.finding: Crew is a distinct local or user-hosted Gateway agent with persistent sessions, schedules, memory and a task runner.

evidence.title: Local command sandbox
evidence.finding: Kiro's optional local sandbox covers shell commands/children and optionally stdio MCP, excluding the agent and built-in file tools.

evidence.title: Privacy and security
evidence.finding: Supervised mode reviews file changes after writes and can revert them; it is explicitly not a security boundary.

evidence.title: Kiro pricing
evidence.locator: Plan cards; pooling; trial FAQ checked 7 November 2026
evidence.finding: Free has fifty credits; paid individual tiers and pooled team seats differ in included credits. Add-ons cost $0.04/credit and taxes are excluded.

evidence.title: Crew Agent Backends
evidence.finding: Developer Mode enables Preview selection of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi and other harnesses. Existing sessions retain their backend. Pi lacks Crew MCP tools; Codex requires sandboxing; Claude preapproved calls may bypass Crew audit.

evidence.title: Crew Task Runner
evidence.locator: Loop; Task IDs; Recovery; Approval gates; Dependencies
evidence.finding: Crew decomposes Markdown specs into persistent task runs and step sessions. Up to three runs/parallel steps, per-run IDs/branches/worktrees, test/review/retry checkpoints, restart reconciliation and explicit approval gates are documented.

evidence.title: Requirements-First Specs
evidence.finding: Kiro generates requirements.md with acceptance criteria, design.md with architecture and testing strategy, and tasks.md with dependencies and optional/required work. Humans review and refine each phase.

evidence.title: Analyze Requirements
evidence.finding: IDE/CLI requirements analysis identifies logical contradictions, ambiguities, conflicting constraints and missing cases. Chat answers update requirements.md. Web does not yet offer this analysis.

evidence.title: Kiro Memory
evidence.finding: Memory is stored locally per user account and shared by IDE/CLI on the machine. It defaults off in IDE and has read-only/learn controls. Current subagents can read parent memory but cannot modify it.

evidence.title: Kiro Data Protection
evidence.finding: Individual/free usage may supply content for improvement by default. IDE/CLI telemetry and content have separate opt-outs. Enterprise improvement collection is off; admin reports remain separately controlled. Free inputs may be held up to sixty days for abuse detection.

evidence.title: Kiro License
evidence.finding: Kiro IDE and CLI are AWS Content under AWS agreements and the AWS IP License. Chromium is the IDE engine; Bun powers the CLI frontend. Dependency licenses do not license the main application as open source.

evidence.title: Crew Running 24/7
evidence.finding: Crew Gateway can run as a service or in Docker on user hardware, including an always-on remote Linux host while the laptop sleeps. Sandbox availability is checked before container agent execution.

evidence.title: Kiro Authentication
evidence.finding: IDE, CLI, Web and Mobile support IAM Identity Center or organization identity providers such as Okta/Entra. CLI also has a CI/headless API-key path.

evidence.title: Kiro Privacy and Security
evidence.finding: IDE supervised mode presents agent file changes for human review and approval, but is explicitly not a sandbox or access-control boundary.

evidence.title: Kiro Mobile availability
evidence.finding: Android is publicly available through Google Play for Android 10+. iPhone requires requested early access through TestFlight; the request page says only limited invitees receive access. Both use paid-plan cloud sessions.

evidence.title: Crew phone browser access
evidence.locator: Reach it from a laptop or phone; named HTTPS tunnel; lines 236-433
evidence.finding: The shipped gateway documents opening its HTTPS dashboard URL on a phone, including a named tunnel or Tailscale Serve token link. This is the user-hosted Crew browser client, distinct from the native Kiro Mobile app.

evidence.title: Crew external harness authentication
evidence.locator: AgentAuthDeclaration for Codex and Claude Code, lines 503-551
evidence.finding: Codex uses its own .codex/auth.json and native sign-in; Claude Code uses its own .claude/.credentials.json and native terminal sign-in. Both are own_credential_file entitlements, independent of Crew Kiro logout. This establishes reuse of each coding agent account through its native harness rather than an API-key-only wrapper.

evidence.title: Shared Crew human prompt admission
evidence.locator: Chat prompt payload and admit_chat_turn; collab.py presence; attribution.py sender_line
evidence.finding: Shipped chat admission records the verified actor with each prompt. The presence model distinguishes principals in one session and attribution labels multiple human authors in the same session. preview.py permits the owner to enable this released opt-in preview; this is distinct people sharing one Crew, not just same-account device access.

evidence.title: Crew 0.12.0 release
evidence.locator: November 5: More Coding Agents; Previews You Can Turn On
evidence.finding: The public release removes Developer Mode, adds Strands and GitHub Copilot CLI, exposes provider keys in Settings Secrets, and ships Shared Crew as a preview owners can switch on to admit other people over Tailscale with equal access.

evidence.title: Kiro harness architecture
evidence.finding: The engineering explanation says the same standalone harness runs on a laptop or inside a VM in the cloud; remote clients connect to its cloud sandbox. This establishes VM execution, not tested containment guarantees.

evidence.title: Kiro team administration
evidence.locator: Teams; shared credit pools and enterprise controls
evidence.finding: The complete pricing page distinguishes organization administrators who manage users, groups, pooled credit limits and access from assigned members. This establishes organization-level administrative roles, without claiming Crew fine-grained per-person roles from a proposal.

evidence.title: Crew fixed native harness registry
evidence.finding: The released runtime has a closed known-backend set for Kiro, Claude Code, KAS, Strands, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Goose, DeepSeek and Copilot. Registration rejects a backend outside that set. Edition plugin registration does not supply a generic arbitrary coding-harness adapter; configured MCP tool commands are a separate feature.

memory.answer: Kiro can retain learned commands, corrections and debugging insights across sessions when enabled.

freshness.answer: Memories can be refined during later work; automatic expiry is not established.

conflict_detection.answer: Requirements analysis finds cross-requirement contradictions and conflicting constraints.

review_enforcement.answer: Analysis is optional and can be skipped; it is not a mandatory delivery gate.

create.answer: Crew Projects creates task runs from a prompt or uploaded spec.

reopen.answer: An interrupted run can resume with passed/skipped steps preserved.

explicit_dispatch.answer: Run starts the task, while pause/cancel controls are available in its sidebar.

task_session_separation.answer: A task run persists across fresh per-step sessions and reviewer sessions.

metadata.answer: Run records include task_id, step attempts, work directory and branch.

durable_states.answer: Step states include PENDING, REVIEWING and PASSED; checkpointed progress survives restart.

read.answer: Task Runner injects the spec, working memory and prior Git state into each step.

create.answer: The runner decomposes the spec into steps with acceptance criteria and dependencies.

state_changes.answer: Steps transition through REVIEWING to PASSED or retry/failure.

dependencies.answer: Task steps declare dependencies for parallel execution.

results.answer: Passed steps create Git commits; reviewer sessions inspect actual diffs.

human_visibility.answer: The dashboard shows task progress, step status, approval buttons and pause/cancel controls.

persistent_requirements.answer: Feature specs persist requirements.md, design.md and tasks.md.

human_edits.answer: Humans refine user stories, acceptance criteria, design and task priorities.

agent_edits.answer: Kiro generates and refines the specification documents.

approvals.answer: The Requirements-First workflow requests user confirmation before advancing phases.

implementation_links.answer: tasks.md contains executable implementation tasks derived from requirements/design.

drift_detection.answer: Analysis can be rerun after requirements edits; automatic implementation-to-spec drift enforcement was not established.

review_integration.answer: Requirements analysis streams issues with suggested fixes and updates requirements.md from answers.

branch.answer: Each task uses its own kirocrew/task/ branch.

worktree.answer: Existing repositories get a separate Git worktree per task run.

container.answer: Crew documents a Docker container runtime with its own persistent volumes and optional inner sandbox.

code_separation.answer: Worktree-based task runs leave the original checkout untouched.

worker_crash.answer: Task Runner reconciles interrupted steps after a Gateway restart.

service_restart.answer: Git-coordinated runs resume automatically from checkpoints after Gateway restart.

state_reconstruction.answer: Passed/skipped steps are retained; unfinished safe steps get a new attempt.

duplicate_actions.answer: Runs without Git/idempotency safeguards reopen paused with an unknown-side-effect notice.

manual_repair.answer: Humans inspect external state before resuming unsafe interrupted runs.

time_limits.answer: kirocrew run --timeout sets a run timeout.

retries.answer: Each step allows three logic/test retries, two crash recoveries and two replans.

enforcement.answer: The runner caps total tasks including replans at fifty and detects repeated-error loops.

concurrency.answer: Crew allows three concurrent task runs and parallel batches of three independent steps.

queues.answer: The shared scheduling queue is persisted in tasks.db.

cancellation.answer: CLI or dashboard can cancel a specific task or all tasks.

recovery.answer: Interrupted steps are reconciled against the Gateway incarnation and retry safety.

sso.answer: Organization sign-in supports IAM Identity Center or external IdP such as Okta and Microsoft Entra.

plan_scope.answer: Organization-managed access uses its admin-provided start URL/region or external identity-provider flow.

delivery.answer: Spec force_approval gates can protect deployment/publish steps.

allow.answer: The task pauses and shows Approve/Deny controls before a forced-approval step.

deny.answer: A forced approval gate can be denied in the dashboard.

enforcement.answer: Claude Code tools preapproved in Claude settings can bypass Crew approval, deny and audit observation. Codex refuses to start with Crew sandbox off.

change_understanding.answer: IDE supervised mode shows agent-generated file changes for review.

shipping_guidance.answer: Turn-completion review must be distinguished from a merge/deployment authorization gate.

tests.answer: Task steps run tests before committing unless --no-test is selected.

independent_review.answer: A separate reviewer session checks the actual Git diff.

failure_blocking.answer: Review failures revert/retry, but reviewer exceptions are treated as passed and tests may be skipped.

configured_policy.answer: force_approval gates and --no-test configure distinct run behaviors.

enforced_policy.answer: force_approval blocks execution even under YOLO, with explicit Approve/Deny buttons.

retained_evidence.answer: Per-step commits and Git log/diff state feed later step prompts.

rollback.answer: A failed independent review reverts the step commit before retry.

client_license.answer: Kiro IDE and CLI use the AWS Content and AWS IP License terms.

source_visibility.answer: Kiro provides dependency-source attribution and relinking material; a complete open-source IDE/CLI was not established.

self_hosting.answer: The Crew Gateway and dashboard run locally, in Docker or on a user-controlled remote host; Kiro/model-service credentials remain backend-specific.

vendor_dependencies.answer: Crew runtime/state are user-hosted, while selected coding harness and provider authentication may depend on external services.

history_portability.answer: IDE/CLI on one machine share local memory, distinct from cross-device transcript export.

code_data.answer: Improvement content can include generated code, questions, other inputs and responses.

retention.answer: Free-tier inputs may be retained up to sixty days for abuse detection; model-specific retention may also apply.

training.answer: Free and individual subscriber content can improve services or models unless opted out; enterprise content is excluded from service improvement.

telemetry_disclosure.answer: Usage telemetry includes interaction, errors and metrics, separate from shared improvement content.

telemetry_defaults.answer: Individual/free usage analytics, errors/crashes and improvement content are collected by default.

telemetry_controls.answer: IDE unchecks Usage Analytics and Performance Metrics; CLI toggles Telemetry off. Content-sharing controls are separate. Enterprise reports are admin controlled.

provider_separation.answer: Model-specific abuse-retention requirements remain separate from Kiro improvement opt-out.
